terms.gloss: a rechargeable battery, as in a phone, a laptop or a car
terms.comment: What Italian and German call accumulatore and Akku: the battery that is filled again and again.

terms.gloss: a cell, the battery one takes out and replaces
evidence: M-O s.v. battery (the Vatican lexicon, Helfer, Egger)
terms.comment: Volta’s own name for his “pile” of plates. Pīla, a pillar, differs from pila, a ball, only in its long vowel.

phrases.english: The batteries are dead; put new ones in.

sources: Lewis & Short: pila · Lewis & Short: pyxis
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 277.
David Morgan and Patrick Owens, Adumbratio Lexici Anglico-Latini, s.v. battery.
